quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Priority Call] Whenever her younger brother calls, Yasmin puts her own work aside immediately and talks to him for as long as he needs, even during her busiest weeks at the clinic. Her colleagues have learned not to schedule anything during those calls.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Yasmin's relationship with her brother?
options: She considers her brother a high priority in her life.
She rarely speaks with her brother.
She resents her brother's phone calls.
She only answers his calls when convenient.
quests.correctAnswer: She considers her brother a high priority in her life.
quests.hint: Think about what dropping everything for someone, no matter how busy she is, reveals about her priorities.
quests.explanation: Setting aside her work every time, even during busy weeks, shows that Yasmin values her brother highly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Below Target] After the department's quarterly numbers came in below target for the second time, the director scheduled one-on-one meetings with every team lead and asked each to bring a plan for the next quarter.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the director's reaction to the numbers?
options: She is taking active steps to address the underperformance.
She believes the numbers exceeded expectations.
She has decided to close the department.
She is ignoring the disappointing results.
quests.correctAnswer: She is taking active steps to address the underperformance.
quests.hint: Think about what scheduling meetings and requesting plans suggests about her intentions.
quests.explanation: Meeting with every team lead and requesting improvement plans shows the director is actively responding to the weak results.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Sharing the Credit] Instead of turning in the group project with his teammates' names removed, Diego insists on listing everyone, even though he did most of the work himself over the weekend.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Diego's character?
options: He did not contribute to the project at all.
He wants all the credit for himself.
He values fairness and giving credit to others.
He dislikes his teammates.
quests.correctAnswer: He values fairness and giving credit to others.
quests.hint: Think about why someone would insist on crediting others despite doing extra work.
quests.explanation: Choosing to list everyone's name despite doing most of the work himself shows Diego values fairness toward his teammates.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Choosing the Middle Bottle] The shopper compares three brands of olive oil, reading the back label of each one closely, before finally choosing the middle-priced bottle instead of the cheapest or the most expensive.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the shopper's approach?
options: She always buys the most expensive option available.
She only cares about spending the least money possible.
She wants good value rather than simply the lowest price.
She chose the bottle at random without looking at anything.
quests.correctAnswer: She wants good value rather than simply the lowest price.
quests.hint: Think about why someone would research carefully and still avoid both extremes.
quests.explanation: Reading labels closely and picking neither the cheapest nor priciest bottle suggests she is looking for the best overall value.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Tasting the Sauce] The chef tastes the sauce, adds a pinch of salt, tastes it again, and only then allows it to be served to the dining room.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the chef?
options: He is careful about the quality of his food.
He never checks his food before serving it.
He dislikes cooking sauces.
He is serving food that is already ruined.
quests.correctAnswer: He is careful about the quality of his food.
quests.hint: Think about what tasting and adjusting a dish more than once shows about someone's standards.
quests.explanation: Tasting the sauce twice and adjusting it before serving shows that the chef holds himself to a high standard of quality.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Convenient Hotel] Even though her flight lands after midnight, Camille books a hotel within walking distance of the conference center rather than one that is cheaper but a twenty-minute taxi ride away.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Camille's priorities for this trip?
options: She values convenience over saving a small amount of money.
She dislikes attending the conference.
She has an unlimited travel budget.
She plans to skip the conference entirely.
quests.correctAnswer: She values convenience over saving a small amount of money.
quests.hint: Think about what choosing a nearby hotel over a cheaper, farther one suggests about her priorities.
quests.explanation: Choosing the closer, pricier hotel for a late arrival suggests Camille prioritizes convenience above saving a little money.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Change in Diet] The nutritionist notices that Mr. Choi's energy levels dropped around the same time he switched to a diet with almost no vegetables, and she suggests he add them back gradually.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the nutritionist's view of the diet change?
options: She suspects the lack of vegetables may be linked to his low energy.
She believes vegetables are unrelated to his energy.
She wants him to remove even more vegetables.
She thinks his low energy is a coincidence with no cause.
quests.correctAnswer: She suspects the lack of vegetables may be linked to his low energy.
quests.hint: Notice the timing between the diet change and the drop in energy, and what she recommends afterward.
quests.explanation: Recommending he add vegetables back right after noting his energy dropped when he removed them suggests she sees a likely connection.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Free Version] The new fitness app locks half its features behind a monthly fee, but reviewers note that the free version still covers everything a beginner would realistically need.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the free version of the app?
options: It contains more features than the paid version.
It is likely sufficient for someone just starting out.
It is only useful for advanced athletes.
It offers nothing of value to any user.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely sufficient for someone just starting out.
quests.hint: Think about what 'everything a beginner would realistically need' suggests about the free tier's usefulness.
quests.explanation: Reviewers noting the free version covers a beginner's needs suggests it works well for those just starting out, even without paying.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Mysterious Emoji] Halfway through the season finale, viewers flood social media with theories, and the show's official account posts only a single mysterious emoji in response.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the show's official account?
options: It is intentionally avoiding confirming or denying the theories.
It fully confirmed every fan theory.
It denied all of the fan theories clearly.
It has stopped posting on social media.
quests.correctAnswer: It is intentionally avoiding confirming or denying the theories.
quests.hint: Think about what posting something vague, instead of a clear answer, suggests about intent.
quests.explanation: Responding with only a mysterious emoji, rather than a clear answer, suggests the account is deliberately keeping fans guessing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [After the Flood] After the flood damaged a dozen homes on the block, neighbors who barely spoke before began organizing supply drop-offs and taking turns checking on the elderly residents.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the effect of the flood on the neighborhood?
options: It had no impact on how neighbors interacted.
It brought the neighbors closer together.
It caused the neighbors to avoid each other.
It made the neighbors compete against one another.
quests.correctAnswer: It brought the neighbors closer together.
quests.hint: Think about how the neighbors' behavior changed after the flood compared to before it.
quests.explanation: Neighbors who barely spoke before now working together suggests the flood brought the community closer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Same Ending] Every time her father tells a story from his childhood, he adds a slightly different detail, yet the ending is always exactly the same triumphant moment.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the story's ending for her father?
options: It is the part of the story that matters most to him.
It is a part he wants to forget.
He dislikes discussing his childhood at all.
It changes every time he tells it.
quests.correctAnswer: It is the part of the story that matters most to him.
quests.hint: Think about what staying constant, even while other details shift, suggests about importance.
quests.explanation: Keeping the same ending every time, while other details vary, suggests that moment holds special meaning for him.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A New Employee's Shifts] The new employee is given the least desirable shifts for the first month, but by the second month, her schedule matches everyone else's on the team.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the workplace's approach to new employees?
options: Experienced employees receive worse shifts than new hires.
Schedules never change from month to month.
New employees are expected to prove themselves before receiving equal treatment.
New employees always get the best shifts immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: New employees are expected to prove themselves before receiving equal treatment.
quests.hint: Think about what changes between the first month and the second month for the new employee.
quests.explanation: Starting with less desirable shifts and then transitioning to equal treatment suggests new hires go through an initial adjustment period.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Single Question Mark] The teacher returns every essay with detailed comments in the margins, but Priya's paper comes back with only a single word circled and a small question mark beside it.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Priya's essay?
options: The teacher found one specific point that needed clarification.
The essay had no issues whatsoever.
The teacher gave up on grading it.
The teacher did not read the essay at all.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher found one specific point that needed clarification.
quests.hint: Think about what a single circled word with a question mark usually signals, compared to no comments at all.
quests.explanation: A circled word with a question mark suggests the teacher noticed one specific point in Priya's essay that needed clarifying.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Reading the Fine Print] The customer asks to see the return policy printed on paper instead of trusting the clerk's verbal explanation, then reads every line before agreeing to the purchase.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the customer?
options: She trusts every salesperson completely.
She wants to be certain of the details before committing.
She plans to return the item immediately.
She has no interest in the return policy.
quests.correctAnswer: She wants to be certain of the details before committing.
quests.hint: Think about why someone would ask for something in writing rather than accepting a verbal answer.
quests.explanation: Asking for the policy in writing and reading it fully suggests the customer wants to be sure of the details before buying.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Shrinking Portion] The food critic orders the same dish on three separate visits to the restaurant, noting that the portion size shrinks slightly each time while the price stays the same.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the restaurant's dish?
options: The dish has remained completely unchanged.
The price has been dropping with each visit.
The portion size has been growing steadily.
Customers are getting less food for the same money over time.
quests.correctAnswer: Customers are getting less food for the same money over time.
quests.hint: Compare what happens to the portion size with what happens to the price across the three visits.
quests.explanation: A shrinking portion at the same price across three visits suggests customers are receiving less value for their money over time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Changed Route] The tour guide changes the group's route at the last minute, leading them away from the main square and mentioning only that 'today is not a good day to go that way.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the main square today?
options: The group specifically requested to avoid crowds.
Something there may make it unsuitable to visit right now.
The guide has never been to the main square.
It is the best possible place to visit today.
quests.correctAnswer: Something there may make it unsuitable to visit right now.
quests.hint: Think about why a guide would avoid a usual route without giving full details.
quests.explanation: Changing the route at the last minute and giving only a vague reason suggests something about the square makes it unsuitable to visit today.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Tracking Salt Intake] Since Mr. Diallo started tracking his meals in an app, he has noticed he eats far more salt than he realized, and his doctor has asked him to bring the log to his next appointment.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the food tracking app?
options: It confirmed exactly what he already expected.
It has no connection to his health.
It revealed a habit Mr. Diallo was not fully aware of.
It only tracks sugar, not salt.
quests.correctAnswer: It revealed a habit Mr. Diallo was not fully aware of.
quests.hint: Think about what 'far more than he realized' suggests about his awareness before using the app.
quests.explanation: Discovering he eats more salt than he realized shows the app revealed a habit that had gone unnoticed before.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Cautious Robot] The delivery robot pauses at the curb, rotates in a small circle, and then reverses back the way it came instead of crossing the street.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the robot?
options: It successfully completed its delivery.
It ran out of battery completely.
It likely detected something preventing it from crossing safely.
It was designed to never cross streets.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely detected something preventing it from crossing safely.
quests.hint: Think about why a delivery robot would turn around instead of continuing on its route.
quests.explanation: Pausing, turning, and reversing instead of crossing suggests the robot's sensors detected an obstacle or unsafe condition.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Take Eleven] The director reshoots the same scene eleven times, and the lead actress later tells an interviewer that take eleven finally 'felt true.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the first ten takes?
options: They were better than the eleventh take.
They were never actually filmed.
They were all considered perfect.
They did not fully satisfy the director or actress.
quests.correctAnswer: They did not fully satisfy the director or actress.
quests.hint: Think about why they would need eleven attempts if the earlier ones felt right.
quests.explanation: Needing eleven takes before it 'felt true' suggests the earlier attempts fell short of what they were aiming for.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Place at the Table] Grandma sets a place at the table for her grandson every Friday, even during the years he lived abroad and could not visit.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Grandma's habit?
options: She forgot that he had moved away.
It is a way of keeping him present in her mind and heart.
She expected him to arrive unannounced every week.
She stopped caring about him while he was abroad.
quests.correctAnswer: It is a way of keeping him present in her mind and heart.
quests.hint: Think about what continuing a habit, even when the person cannot be there, usually reveals.
quests.explanation: Setting a place for him even while he lived abroad suggests Grandma kept him close in spirit, even when he could not physically be there.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Ahead of Schedule] The team celebrates hitting their sales target three days before the end of the month, then keeps working at the same pace instead of easing off.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the team's attitude toward their work?
options: They plan to stop working for the rest of the month.
They missed their sales target completely.
They are satisfied with doing the bare minimum.
They aim to exceed expectations, not just meet them.
quests.correctAnswer: They aim to exceed expectations, not just meet them.
quests.hint: Think about what continuing at full pace, after already reaching the goal, suggests about their ambition.
quests.explanation: Continuing to work hard after already reaching the target suggests the team wants to exceed expectations rather than just meet them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Long Return Line] The store's return line is twice as long the week after the holiday sale as it was during the sale itself.
quests.question: What can be inferred about some of the holiday purchases?
options: No one shopped during the sale.
The store stopped accepting returns after the sale.
Every item purchased was kept by its buyer.
A number of the items bought were later returned.
quests.correctAnswer: A number of the items bought were later returned.
quests.hint: Think about what a long return line right after a big sale usually indicates.
quests.explanation: A return line twice as long right after the sale suggests many of the purchased items ended up being returned.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [First in a Decade] The principal invites the debate team to present at the school assembly after they place first at the regional competition for the first time in a decade.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the debate team's recent achievement?
options: It is a notable and rare accomplishment for the school.
It happens every single year without exception.
It was a minor, unremarkable result.
The team has always placed first regularly.
quests.correctAnswer: It is a notable and rare accomplishment for the school.
quests.hint: Think about what 'first time in a decade' reveals about how unusual this result is.
quests.explanation: Winning for the first time in ten years, and being invited to present at assembly, shows this is a rare and notable achievement.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Hiring a Translator] The community center adds a translator to its front desk after receptionists mention struggling to help several visitors each week.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the visitors the receptionists struggled to help?
options: They likely spoke a different language than the staff.
They never actually visited the center.
They were fluent in the same language as the staff.
They were staff members themselves.
quests.correctAnswer: They likely spoke a different language than the staff.
quests.hint: Think about what kind of difficulty would be solved specifically by hiring a translator.
quests.explanation: Adding a translator to solve a recurring front-desk difficulty suggests the visitors likely spoke a different language than the staff.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Jeans That Fit Again] After cutting out late-night snacks for a month, Mr. Alavi mentions to his sister that his jeans finally fit the way they used to two years ago.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the effect of cutting out late-night snacks?
options: It made his clothes fit more loosely than before.
It caused him to gain weight rapidly.
It had no effect on his body at all.
It appears to have helped him lose some weight.
quests.correctAnswer: It appears to have helped him lose some weight.
quests.hint: Think about what jeans fitting better, right after this change, suggests about his body.
quests.explanation: His jeans fitting the way they used to, right after cutting out late-night snacks, suggests the change helped him lose weight.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Beating the Rush] The food truck outside the office sells out of tacos by 12:30 every day, so Layla has started setting a reminder to walk over at 11:45 instead of her usual noon break.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Layla's reminder?
options: She is trying to avoid the food truck entirely.
She wants to arrive after the truck closes.
She no longer enjoys eating tacos.
She wants to make sure she gets tacos before they run out.
quests.correctAnswer: She wants to make sure she gets tacos before they run out.
quests.hint: Think about the connection between the truck selling out early and her new, earlier reminder.
quests.explanation: Setting an earlier reminder because the truck sells out by 12:30 suggests Layla is trying to beat the rush and get tacos before they run out.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Busy Phone Lines] The travel agency's phone lines are busy for hours after the government announces new visa rules for a popular destination.
quests.question: What can be inferred about travelers' reaction to the new visa rules?
options: Travelers are completely unaffected by the announcement.
Many travelers have questions or concerns about the change.
No one is interested in that destination anymore.
The phone lines are busy for an unrelated reason.
quests.correctAnswer: Many travelers have questions or concerns about the change.
quests.hint: Think about what busy phone lines right after the announcement suggest about public interest.
quests.explanation: Phone lines staying busy for hours right after the visa announcement suggest many travelers have questions about how it affects them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Rolling Back an Update] The company quietly rolls back its newest app update after social media fills with complaints about the redesigned menu within the first day.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the app update?
options: It was not well received by users.
It was praised by nearly everyone.
It was planned to be temporary from the start.
It had no effect on the app's design.
quests.correctAnswer: It was not well received by users.
quests.hint: Think about why a company would reverse a change so quickly after releasing it.
quests.explanation: Rolling back the update right after a wave of complaints suggests the redesign was not well received by users.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Resale Prices Triple] Ticket resale prices for the festival triple within a week of the lineup announcement, even though tickets are still technically available at face value.
quests.question: What can be inferred about interest in the festival?
options: No one wants to attend the festival.
It has dropped sharply since the announcement.
It is much higher than the original ticket supply anticipated.
The festival has been cancelled.
quests.correctAnswer: It is much higher than the original ticket supply anticipated.
quests.hint: Think about why resale prices would rise so quickly if tickets are still officially available.
quests.explanation: Resale prices tripling despite tickets still being available suggests demand is much higher than organizers expected.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Double-Checking the Figures] The manager praises the team's report in the group meeting but later asks Sofia privately to double-check two of the figures before it goes out.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the two figures the manager mentioned?
options: The manager is completely certain they are correct.
The manager may have some doubts about their accuracy.
The manager wants them removed from the report entirely.
The manager has never looked at the report.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager may have some doubts about their accuracy.
quests.hint: Think about why the manager would raise this privately rather than during the group praise.
quests.explanation: Asking privately to double-check specific figures, right after praising the report publicly, suggests the manager has some lingering doubt about those numbers.
